endorsements.quote: Students receive clear information about AI use, data collection, access, limitations, and any influence on learning or assessment.
Identifiable information is not entered into unapproved general-purpose AI systems.
Authorization specifies modality, purpose, storage, access, retention, and deletion; technical controls include encryption and access logging.
A re-identification and child-rights risk assessment precedes use of de-identified audiovisual material.
Child-related recordings are not used for model training, fine-tuning, or vendor product improvement without separate authorization and institutional review.
Governance also addresses data leakage, prompt injection, insecure integrations, malicious inputs, and misuse of exported content.

A named safeguarding lead may pause activities that raise child-protection concerns; a privacy lead oversees authorization and data handling; and a system owner is accountable for validation, monitoring, and change control.
Material changes to models, prompts, scenarios, rubrics, data pipelines, interfaces, or intended uses undergo proportionate revalidation and controlled change management.

A joint governance body includes education and childcare leaders, educators or mentors, student representatives, and relevant family, child-rights, safeguarding, privacy, technical, or developmental expertise.
Vendor agreements cover documentation, data handling, subprocessors, security, limitations, material-change and breach notification, audit cooperation, and secure exit.
Audit trails record system versions, authorized input provenance, consequential outputs, and human decisions.
Incident procedures specify reportable events, severity, responsibilities, containment, notification, remediation, and escalation.
Advancement depends on evidence of educational value, safety, equity, workload, and feasibility before data sensitivity, technical complexity, or proximity to practice increases.
Consequential outputs are reviewed against multiple evidence sources.
It may support scenario generation, evidence organization, formative feedback, and reflection, while qualified educators and childcare mentors retain final authority.
Readiness and progression decisions are explainable, contestable, and subject to human review.
A validated benchmark is rerun after material updates and at defined intervals; threshold breaches trigger revalidation, restriction, rollback, or suspension.
Reviewer names, roles, conflicts, and independent ratings are recorded; vendor review alone is insufficient.

Assessment can require students to recognize hallucinated or fabricated content, verify feedback against observation and professional standards, resist automation bias, identify concealed uncertainty or role overreach, refuse to enter identifiable child or family data into unapproved systems, and explain AI limitations to mentors or families.

Real child- or family-related data require documented educational necessity, an appropriate lawful basis, institutional approval, restricted access, defined retention, secure storage, and verifiable deletion.

Technical controls are proportionate to risk and data sensitivity and may include role-based access, strong authentication, encryption, secure configuration, vulnerability testing, backup, rollback, and incident response.
Accessible interfaces, language support, equivalent non-AI task formats, and reasonable participation alternatives help separate the target competence from digital familiarity.
Data use follows necessity, proportionality, minimization, purpose limitation, and child-centred protection.

unlisted_practices: Do not use AI to diagnose, label, or infer a child's emotional or mental state from behavioral, visual, vocal, or contextual signals.
Do not allow AI to autonomously certify competence, determine readiness, or make other high-stakes decisions such as excluding students from practicum.
Review synthetic infant- or toddler-like media through a documented human developmental-fidelity gate with independent expert reviewers before instructional use.
Prefer lower-risk non-AI educational alternatives where they achieve equivalent outcomes, introducing GenAI only when it shows incremental educational value.
Preserve students' rights to inspect evidence, correct inaccuracies, and appeal AI-influenced decisions without retaliation.
Require separate lawful justification and independent review before extracting biometric identifiers or facial or voice embeddings.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual framework and perspective article proposing design and governance specifications (including human supervision and developmental fidelity gates) for multimodal generative AI simulations in childcare/mental health education.
